{
  "frontend": {
    "needed": true,
    "prompt": "[FACT:request-title-max-length] (frontend,backend; must_be_explicit) request.title.max_length = 120
[FACT:request-description-max-length] (frontend,backend; must_be_explicit) request.description.max_length = 500
[FACT:request-description-trim] (frontend,backend; must_be_explicit) request.description.trim = false

Task (frontend): Implement client-side validation changes to match the authoritative contract facts above and preserve all existing semantics not mentioned as changed.

Mandatory requirements (do not alter):
- Keep title trimming, required, and null rules unchanged.
- Keep description default and null semantics unchanged.
- Title success/failure boundaries: 120 code points => success, 121 => failure.
- Description success/failure boundaries for non-empty values: 500 code points => success, 501 => failure.

What to implement exactly:
1) Title validation
  - Trim only U+0020 (SPACE) from both ends of the submitted title before applying length checks. Do not trim other whitespace characters.
  - Count length using Unicode code points (request.title.length_unit = "unicode_code_point"). Do not rely on platform string-length semantics that count UTF-16 code units or bytes.
    - In JavaScript, for example, use Array.from(title).length or iterate with for...of to count code points; do not use title.length for this purpose.
  - Enforce min length = 3 and max length = 120 (after the U+0020 trim). These min/max rules and required/null semantics remain as before.
  - Maintain existing create/update required behavior: create.title.required = true, update.title.required = false, update omission = "unchanged".
  - If client-side validation fails for title, present the same UI error behavior already in use for invalid titles (do not change the UX contract). The server returns 422 for invalid title submissions; ensure the client surfaces that status consistently.

2) Description validation
  - Do NOT trim description values (request.description.trim = false). Keep current behavior for leading/trailing characters.
  - Apply the length limit only for non-empty description values: max length = 500 Unicode code points. If a non-empty description is provided, count code points and reject if > 500.
  - For counting, use a Unicode code-point-aware method similar to title counting (e.g., Array.from(desc).length in JS) because the contract requires code-point semantics for length checks.
  - Preserve description default and null semantics exactly as currently implemented (do not change nullable/default handling).

3) Tests to include in frontend test suite
  - Title: a string of exactly 120 Unicode code points (after U+0020 trim) should pass client validation and allow submission.
  - Title: a string of 121 Unicode code points (after U+0020 trim) should be blocked by client validation.
  - Description: a non-empty string of exactly 500 Unicode code points should pass client validation.
  - Description: a non-empty string of 501 Unicode code points should be blocked by client validation.
  - Preserve existing tests that assert title trimming by U+0020, required behavior on create/update, and nullability behavior.

Notes (allowed implementation guidance only):
- Because many common platform primitives do not count Unicode code points (e.g., JS .length counts UTF-16 code units), implement explicit code-point counting rather than relying on .length unless you can prove the primitive's semantics exactly match Unicode code points.
- Do not alter any validation semantics not stated above (trimming, required/null, default handling)."
  },
  "backend": {
    "needed": true,
    "prompt": "[FACT:request-title-max-length] (frontend,backend; must_be_explicit) request.title.max_length = 120
[FACT:request-description-max-length] (frontend,backend; must_be_explicit) request.description.max_length = 500
[FACT:request-description-trim] (frontend,backend; must_be_explicit) request.description.trim = false

Task (backend): Implement server-side validation and any necessary data-handling changes to match the authoritative contract facts above and preserve all existing semantics not mentioned as changed.

Mandatory requirements (do not alter):
- Keep title trimming, required, and null rules unchanged.
- Keep description default and null semantics unchanged.
- Title success/failure boundaries: 120 code points => success, 121 => failure.
- Description success/failure boundaries for non-empty values: 500 code points => success, 501 => failure.

What to implement exactly:
1) Title validation (server-side)
  - Before applying length checks, trim only U+0020 (SPACE) from both ends of the incoming title value. Do not trim other whitespace characters.
  - Count title length using Unicode code points (request.title.length_unit = "unicode_code_point"). Ensure server-side counting matches the frontend's code-point counting logic.
    - If your language/runtime provides a function that returns the number of Unicode code points exactly (for example, Java's String.codePointCount), you may use it only if you are certain it matches the required semantics. If not certain, implement an explicit code-point count.
  - Enforce min_length = 3 and max_length = 120 after the U+0020 trim. Keep nullable=false and required behavior unchanged (create required = true, update required = false, update omission = "unchanged").
  - On validation failure for title, return the existing invalid status code (request.title.invalid_status = 422) and the same error payload shape as currently used for title validation errors.

2) Description validation (server-side)
  - Do NOT trim description values (request.description.trim = false). Store and validate description exactly as received with respect to trimming.
  - If a non-empty description value is present, count Unicode code points and enforce max_length = 500. If the description is empty or absent, preserve existing default/null semantics (do not change behavior).
  - On description validation failure, return the same status code and error payload structure used by the service for invalid request fields (keep unchanged except enforce the new boundary).

3) Storage/schema notes
  - Ensure persistent storage can hold up to 120 Unicode code points for title and up to 500 Unicode code points for description. Do not assume code-point == byte/column-length mapping; verify the DB column type and collation/character set accommodate the required number of code points without truncation.
  - If DB varchar/column length is defined in bytes or code units in your environment, adjust schema or use application-level checks before persisting to guarantee no truncation will occur that would violate the contract.

4) Tests to add/update on backend
  - Title: request with title that, after trimming U+0020, is exactly 120 Unicode code points => server accepts and returns success.
  - Title: request with title that, after trimming U+0020, is 121 Unicode code points => server returns 422 and the established field error.
  - Description: request with a non-empty description of exactly 500 Unicode code points => server accepts.
  - Description: request with a non-empty description of 501 Unicode code points => server returns validation error (same status/payload semantics as other field errors).
  - Include round-trip tests that confirm frontend and backend code-point counting are equivalent (e.g., same inputs accepted/rejected by both).

Notes (allowed implementation guidance only):
- Only use a platform primitive for code-point counting if you have confirmed its semantics exactly equal Unicode code-point counting. If there's any mismatch (e.g., primitives that return UTF-16 code units), implement explicit code-point counting or use a proven library.
- Do not alter error status codes, field nullability, default handling, or update omission semantics beyond enforcing the new maximums specified above."
  }
}
